newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana honours dead Nigerian Afrobeat star Fela.
newsitem.headline: Ghana honours dead Nigerian Afrobeat star Fela.

text.p: Scores of Ghanaian artists staged a marathon music concert lasting into the early hours of Monday to honour Nigeria's dead Afrobeat jazz star Fela Anikulapo Kuti.
The 12-hour extravaganza in Accra's Centre for National Culture and organised by the Musicians Union of Ghana attracted thousands of Fela's fans in black or red mourning attire.
On parade were some of Ghana's best known musicians, notably drummer Okeremeh Asante, Mustapha Tetteh Addy and Alex Konadu.
Fela, who became a star of the Nigerian and international music scene in the 1970s and 1980s, died of heart failure related to AIDS on August 2. The composer, singer and saxophonist was 58.
Some of the Ghanaian stars who took turns on stage included close professional associates of Fela, who invented Afrobeat, a pulsating fusion of jazz, West African highlife and calypso.
Fela's son, Femi, took centre-stage in the show'a climax, jamming with the Ghana Broadcasting Corporation band led by his father's one-time collaborator, Stan Plange.
Showing his own versatility on his father's favourite tenor saxophone, Femi brought the crowd to a frenzy as he reeled out some of Fela's top hits -- "Lady", "Palaver" and "Who are You?"
Several thousand Fela fans sang and danced at their idol's burial in a working class district of Lagos on August 12.
